claim: Both language sides asked for the same missing thing this year: a recipe delivered as a hands-free, timed, step-by-step run rather than a block of text. In English a subreddit built it themselves (Parsnip, 139 points in r/cookingforbeginners) and another thread asks for recipes formatted like IKEA manuals; in Chinese the request appears under a developer's open 'you ask, I build' thread, and the developer's reply is that he has no product to point at.
evidence: 283 comments (Xiaohongshu 想要什么软件？你说，我做！, 286 likes)
method: Read a Xiaohongshu thread where a nine-year software engineer publicly takes feature requests and answers each one with whether a product already exists — an unusually clean built-in 'is this solved' filter. He answered the手机控电脑 request with 向日葵/TeamViewer and the停车场 request with a cost objection, but answered the cooking-timer request with 我研究一下. Then checked the English side and found the same request twice, plus a shipped competitor. Cross-referenced the radar index: ⭐#375 (厨房跟做语音助手) already exists there with a one-line 论据 and no voices — this is its evidence.
hook: Someone standing at the stove with raw chicken on their hands, trying to scroll a wall of text with a knuckle, guessing at what 'until fragrant' means.
does: Nothing complete yet. What is wanted: take one recipe and run it — each step spoken aloud, its timer started for you, the next step on your voice, and the vague parts (heat, doneness, quantity) turned into something checkable.
edge: Recipes are written as reference documents and used as live instructions. Nobody has fixed the mismatch; they have only added photos.
why_use: The failure is specific and repeated in both languages: hands are dirty, the screen locks, the timing lives in prose, and the cook improvises and ruins it.
gap: Recipes are still delivered as text blocks, not as hands-free, timed, step-by-step runs with checkable vague parts.
counter: Parsnip already shipped this shape in English with 450 levels and community goodwill behind it, so the English side is not open. In Chinese, 下厨房 owns recipe distribution and can add a step mode in one release. And cooking-app retention is brutal for a reason nobody talks around: most households cook the same eight dishes, so a tool that teaches you to follow a recipe is used hardest by the people who will stop needing it.
differentiator: Do not own a recipe library — that is the part that is already owned and already crowded. Take the recipe the person already found (a screenshot, a Xiaohongshu note, a link, a photo of a cookbook page) and convert that one into a hands-free run: steps read aloud, timers started automatically, advance by voice, and the vague instructions expanded into a checkable cue. The wedge is 'works with whatever recipe you already trust', which is exactly what a platform with its own library will not build. Cold start (Chinese): the comment tree of 「想要什么软件？你说，我做！」 (283 comments) and the 下厨房 App Store review section; Cold start (English): r/cookingforbeginners, the 'recipes as IKEA manuals' thread and its 32 comments.
value: Someone learning to cook, or cooking for a child with a specific diet — a one-off purchase or a small subscription, priced against one ruined dinner.
risk: The people who need it most graduate out of needing it; retention is the whole business and this shape has no answer to it yet.
consumer_angle: An app that turns any recipe into a guided, voice-driven cooking session with automatic timers and visual doneness cues.

zh.claim: 今年两种语言都在要同一件缺席的东西：把菜谱变成一次免手、带计时、一步一步跑完的流程，而不是一整块文字。英文那边一个版块自己把它做出来了（Parsnip，r/cookingforbeginners 139 分），另一帖在问能不能把菜谱排成宜家说明书；中文这边它出现在一位开发者公开征集需求的帖子下，而开发者的回复是他没有现成产品可指。
zh.hook: 一个手上沾着生鸡肉、正用指关节去划一整屏文字的人，还得自己猜「炒香」到底是多久。
zh.does: 目前还没有完整的东西。被要的是：拿一份菜谱，把它跑起来——每一步念出来、计时替你按下、下一步用嘴说、含糊的地方（火候、熟没熟、多少量）变成能对照的判断。
zh.gap: 痛点击中了，但所有产品都在解「存」那一半。菜谱应用比的是谁的菜多；做饭的人的问题是灶台前那二十分钟。中文那条请求把缺的部分点得很准——每一步一个计时器，还要有个东西拦住你别灵机一动——而那位正在接需求的开发者，没有产品可以指给他。
zh.counter: Parsnip 已经把这个形状在英文侧做出来了，450 关，还带着社区好感，所以英文那边不算开着。中文侧下厨房握着菜谱分发，加一个跟做模式就是一个版本的事。而做饭类应用的留存差得有原因，且这原因没人绕得过去：大多数家庭翻来覆去就做那八道菜——一个教你照着菜谱做的工具，用得最狠的正是那批很快就不再需要它的人。
zh.differentiator: 别做菜谱库——那部分已经被人握着而且很挤。拿这个人已经找到的那一份菜谱（截图、小红书笔记、链接、菜谱书拍的一页），只把那一份变成免手跑完的流程：步骤念出来、计时自动起、说一声进下一步、含糊的指令展开成能对照的判断。切口是「你已经信的那份菜谱，它能直接跑」，而这恰好是有自己菜谱库的平台不会做的。冷启动（中文）：「想要什么软件？你说，我做！」那条 283 条评论的评论树，以及下厨房的 App Store 评论区；冷启动（英文）：r/cookingforbeginners 的 recipes as IKEA manuals 帖及其 32 条评论。
zh.value: 正在学做饭的人，或者要给孩子做特定饮食的人——买断或小额订阅，对标「少毁一顿饭」。
zh.risk: 最需要它的人会毕业；留存就是全部生意，而这个形状目前对留存没有答案。
zh.why_use: 失败点很具体，而且在两种语言里重复出现：手是脏的、屏幕会锁、时间信息藏在句子里，于是人开始自由发挥，然后毁掉这道菜。
zh.edge: 菜谱是按参考资料写的，却是被当作现场指令用的。没有人修过这个错配，只是加了更多图。

pick_reason: Verified demand from both English and Chinese communities, clear gap, and a feasible solo build.
